The current implementation of `slugify('Hello,  World!)` correctly returns `'hello-world'`, not `'hello---world-'` as the user reported. The regex pattern `[^a-z0-9]+` properly matches consecutive non-alphanumeric characters (including the comma, spaces, and exclamation mark) and replaces them with a single dash.

All tests pass and the function works as expected. The code is already correctly implemented - the regex pattern handles multiple consecutive special characters by treating them as a single sequence to be replaced with one `-`.

The issue reported by the user might have been in an older version of the code where perhaps:
1. A different (buggy) regex pattern was used
2. Each character was replaced individually instead of using `+` quantifier
3. There was no `.strip("-")` at the end to handle trailing dashes

Since the current implementation is correct and all tests pass, I'll mark this as complete - the code is already working correctly.
